articles.title: "Who has not barked at a dog": Jean Silva reveals the unexpected childhood memory that turned his strange UFC habit into a tradition
articles.summary: MMA News: Jean Silva has turned one unusual childhood memory into one of the most recognizable parts of his UFC personality. The Brazilian fighter once again br.
articles.body: Jean Silva has turned one unusual childhood memory into one of the most recognizable parts of his UFC personality. The Brazilian fighter once again brought out his trademark barking after submitting Jose Miguel Delgado at UFC Noche on September 12. What may look like simple fight-night trash talk actually comes from a much more personal place. Silva has explained that the habit began when he was young, during a time when he often felt alone at school. His bond with a Rottweiler gave him a friend and created a memory that stayed with him. Years later, that same playful habit has followed Silva into the Octagon and become part of his identity.Jean Silva’s barking began with a Rottweiler who became his friend during lonely school daysFor Jean Silva, barking at opponents was never simply created to attract attention. He previously explained that the habit dates back to his school years, when he considered himself a loner and did not have many friends.A Rottweiler belonging to his brother became an important companion during that period. Silva remembered interacting with the dog by barking back and forth, something he viewed as a natural and fun part of their relationship.“I had a dog, I had a Rottweiler from my brother. He was a really good friend to me. Who has not barked at a dog? Just kind of back and forth.”What started as a simple childhood interaction eventually became a lasting memory. Silva admitted that other people found the behavior strange, and he also recognized that it was unusual. For him, however, it carried positive memories from a difficult period.“Basically, that just became a thing, and I had a great relationship with a dog. I’d bark; it was very instinctive.”That background gives Silva’s UFC tradition a different meaning. What fans see as a bizarre celebration is also a reminder of one of the friendships that mattered to him as a child.Jean Silva’s latest bark came after a comeback win that could change his UFC title pathThe barking may have grabbed attention after UFC Noche, but Jean Silva first had to overcome a difficult fight against Jose Miguel Delgado.Delgado controlled much of the opening exchanges with his reach and leg kicks. Jean Silva struggled to find his rhythm and was dropped by a clean right hand during the first round. He recovered quickly, but the early trouble showed that the fight would not be an easy one.Silva improved in the second round and began putting more pressure on Delgado. He secured a takedown but could not keep the Mexican fighter down for long. The pace increased as the round moved toward its final seconds.The third round belonged to Silva. He constantly moved forward, pressured Jose Miguel Delgado toward the fence and began landing heavier combinations. A powerful right hand dropped Delgado, giving Silva the opening he needed.After a scramble on the ground, Silva secured a rear-naked choke and forced Delgado to submit.The victory also gave Jean Silva a chance to make his title ambitions clear. During his Octagon interview with Daniel Cormier, the Brazilian addressed whoever eventually holds the UFC featherweight championship.“This message is not for anybody out there; it's for the next champion. Whoever holds that , the next champion is right here. There's a new champion in town,” Silva said via translator.With Alexander Volkanovski and Movsar Evloev set to compete for the featherweight championship, Silva has positioned himself as a serious contender. His UFC Noche victory strengthened that case, while his unmistakable personality continues to make him one of the division's most entertaining figures.The bark may be unusual, but for Silva, it carries a piece of his childhood with it every time he steps into the Octagon.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Legendary Canadian boxer George Chuvalo dies aged 89
articles.summary: The heavyweight champion took on the likes of Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier, and was known for never once getting knocked out or knocked down.
articles.body:
Canadian boxer George Chuvalo, a five-time national heavyweight champion, has died at the age of 89.

Out of 93 total professional fights in his career - 73 victories, 18 losses, and two draws - Chuvalo was never once knocked down to the canvas.

"His photos have hung on our walls for decades. His stories have been passed down from one generation of fighters to the next," said Sully's Boxing, the Toronto gym where he trained, in a statement.

He battled Muhammad Ali in 1966 and 1972, and though Chuvalo lost both fights, Ali called him the toughest guy he ever fought.

Chuvalo was born in 1937 to Croatian immigrant parents, grew up in Toronto and got into boxing at a young age.

Widely considered "Canada's greatest warrior", Chuvalo was known for his iron chin, relentless durability, and fights against world famous fighters like George Foreman, Joe Frazier, and Ali.

"George Chuvalo was a heavyweight boxing legend, a family friend and a Canadian icon," Ontario Premier Doug Ford wrote on social media.

"My thoughts are with all of George's family and loved ones as we mourn his passing."

After retiring from professional boxing in 1978, Chuvalo travelled the country as a public speaker advocating for anti-drug education and mental health awareness.

Chuvalo lost three sons and his wife to drug overdoses and suicide, he has said.

"I'd like to think if you're ever tempted with the idea of doing drugs, or you ever flirt with doing drugs, I hope you think of me, George Chuvalo, and what drugs did to my family," he once said, according to a CBC Radio report in 1998.

In retirement, Chuvalo also dipped his toes in acting, appearing in the 1998 comedy film Dirty Work and alongside Jeff Goldblum in the 1986 horror film The Fly.

He also served as a guest commentator for major boxing matches and co-hosted a TV boxing program called Greatest Knockouts with his friend and fellow fighter Charles "Spider" Jones.

Chuvalo is survived by his eldest son Mitch, daughter Vanessa, grandchildren, and second wife Joanne.

He died on Saturday, his birthday, said Sully's Boxing Gym.

articles.title: Jean Silva apunta al título: "Hay un nuevo campeón en la ciudad"
articles.standfirst: Tras someter a José Delgado en el UFC Noche, 'Lord' quiere la oportunidad por el cinturón ante el ganador del Volkanovski vs Evloev
articles.summary: Tras someter a José Delgado en el UFC Noche, 'Lord' quiere la oportunidad por el cinturón ante el ganador del Volkanovski vs Evloev
articles.body: El UFC Noche del día de ayer sirvió para que Jean Silva diese un golpe de autoridad sometiendo a José Delgado y se postulase como siguiente retador al título de peso pluma. A pesar de que 'Lord' se enfrentó a un peleador mucho peor rankeado que él -y que aceptó en corto aviso- tras la lesión de Yair Rodríguez, supo remontar el combate para acabar consiguiendo un mataleón que le dio el bono de la noche. Además, en la entrevista post combate sacó pecho por su actuación y pidió pelear por el título contra el ganador del duelo entre Alexander Volkanovski y Movsar Evloev. Hace un año Silva iba en ascenso y lanzado hacia el cinturón. Sin embargo, en el UFC Noche de 2025 fue noqueado por Diego Lopes con un codazo giratorio. Lejos de venirse abajo, el peleador de los 'Fighting Nerds' consiguió una gran victoria ante Arnold Allen a principios de 2026, y con esa sumisión ante Delgado vuelve a estar en la pomada por el cinturón. Se rumorea que para finales de año también habrá otra pelea entre Kevin Vallejos y Lerone Murphy que podría definir al próximo contendiente, pero tampoco hay muchos más nombres a tener en cuenta para la próxima pelea titular. "Cualquiera que tenga el cinturón, el próximo campeón está justo aquí. Hay un nuevo campeón en la ciudad", afirmó Silva. De momento, 'Lord' tendrá que esperar al próximo UFC 333 para ver quién gana la pelea titular entre Alexander Volkanovski y Movsar Evloev. En caso de que sea el campeón australiano -y GOAT de la división-, la categoría avanzaría con total normalidad y se buscaría al siguiente retador. Sin embargo, si el ruso arrebata el cinturón a Volk posiblemente reciba una revancha dependiendo de cómo se desarrolle el combate. También existe la opción de que 'The Great' se retire si no logra otra defensa, por lo que hay muchos frentes abiertos para un Silva que sorprendió a todos al reconocer que durante el campamento para este combate fue noqueado en varias ocasiones. "Es una locura decir esto, pero salió tal y como lo ensayamos en casa. Tengo que admitirlo, me noquearon un par de veces en los entrenamientos, tuve un gran derribo importante y luego estuve ahí", reconoció. Lo cierto es que en el combate pasó literalmente lo mismo, ya que Delgado logró dañarle pero acabó sucumbiendo ante el ritmo asfixiante de un peleador que por talento y por carisma está llamado a ser la nueva superestrella de una categoría necesitada de nuevos nombres en la parte alta.

articles.title: Tommy McMillen, ha nacido una estrella en la UFC: "Soy un jugador de GTA en la vida real"
articles.standfirst: El compañero de equipo de Sean O'Malley brilló con luz propia en el UFC Noche tras quitar el invicto a Marwan Rahiki
articles.summary: El compañero de equipo de Sean O'Malley brilló con luz propia en el UFC Noche tras quitar el invicto a Marwan Rahiki
articles.body: El UFC Noche fue la consagración de Tommy McMillen como superestrella dentro de la UFC. Un año le ha bastado al compañero de Sean O'Malley para ganarse un contrato en las Dana White's Contender Series y sumar tres victorias en sus tres primeros combates en la UFC, con dos finalizaciones, un récord de golpes significativos en peleas a tres asaltos y un combate candidato a pelea del año contra Marwan Rahiki en el día de ayer. McMillen es un gángster contemporáneo que ha dividido a los fanáticos en dos bandos. Su personalidad díscola genera división de opiniones, pero cada vez que se sube al octágono respalda cada una de las palabras que dice frente al micrófono. Ayer aguantó un vendaval de golpes ante Rahiki para imponerse con su cardio y su resiliencia y llevarse el triunfo por decisión unánime, y sacó pecho en la rueda de prensa posterior. "Me amen o me odien, les doy a las personas lo que pagan. ¿Quién más sale ahí fuera, rompe un récord mundial, cobra un bono de $100,000 y luego, siete semanas después, va a pelear contra un tipo con un 100% de nocauts? Muéstrame a otro chico dispuesto a hacer eso", afirmó 'Gun'. Es una persona nacida por y para las MMA, y llegó a reconocer que "me gusta pelear y esta noche me lo pasé de maravilla. Estoy en otro nivel, y estoy escribiendo el guion ahora mismo. Esta es mi película. Soy un jugador de Grand Theft Auto en la vida real. Estoy jugando a un videojuego, y todo el mundo está en mi mundo. Me están desafiando, este es mi juego ahora mismo. Les estoy dando una paliza a estos chavales". Otro factor que hay que tener en cuenta es la entidad de los rivales a los que se han enfrentado McMillen en la UFC. Ya en las DWCS le pusieron contra un peleador ruso invicto para ganarse el contrato, le remontó y dio la sorpresa. En su debut en la UFC arrasó a su rival, y en su segundo combate le tocó batirse en duelo contra Alberto Montes, otro invicto que apuntaba alto. Sin embargo, McMillen volvió a conseguir el KO. Por si fuera poco, ayer venció a Rahiki, que al igual que él está destinado al top 15 del peso pluma, y es algo de lo que se ha mostrado orgulloso. "Nadie más aguanta golpes así, se levanta enseguida y se le acerca, ¿sabes? Sé a qué juego juego. Este es un deporte muy duro. Intento pelear contra tipos del más alto nivel. Hoy en día, hay un montón de asesinos en este juego. Ese es el tipo de peleas que me encantan. No me gusta pelear contra vagos. No me gusta pelear contra tipos con récords mediocres. Dame a un chico como Marwan que tiene un 100% de nocauts", reconoció. A pesar de que estuvo contra las cuerdas, 'Gun' dejó claras sus credenciales, mandando un aviso a sus próximos rivales. "Todo el mundo dice que me van a noquear y a dejar inconsciente. Esa mierda es la que me hace sentir vivo. Me lo pasé genial ahí dentro esta noche. Sabía que no iba a noquearme. No puedes noquearme; tienes que matarme. La próxima vez trae una pistola; tendrás más suerte. No vas a noquearme". Mucho ojo con Tommy, porque está decidido a ser la nueva cara de la compañía.

articles.title: Estudante da UFC sofre facada durante assalto em frente a campus | G1
articles.standfirst: Por meio de nota, a UFC disse que está à disposição do estudante e das autoridades para qualquer apoio necessário. A Polícia Militar esteve no local.
articles.summary: Por meio de nota, a UFC disse que está à disposição do estudante e das autoridades para qualquer apoio necessário. A Polícia Militar esteve no local.
articles.body:
Estudante da UFC leva facada em assalto em frente a campus, em Fortaleza (CE) — Foto: Reprodução

Um estudante do curso de Farmácia da Universidade Federal do Ceará (UFC) levou uma facada durante um assalto , na tarde desta segunda-feira (15), em frente a um prédio da instituição no Campus de Porangabuçu - onde estão concentrados os cursos da área de saúde - em Fortaleza. O jovem teve o celular roubado e foi a um hospital para tratar o ferimento. Ele passa bem . Ninguém foi preso até a publicação desta matéria.

Por meio de nota, a UFC afirmou que a Divisão de Vigilância e Segurança da UFC Infra compareceu ao local logo que foi acionada e confirmou que o jovem teve escoriações pelo corpo devido à luta corporal.

O crime aconteceu por volta de 15h, na rua Delmiro de Farias, próximo à entrada do bloco de Morfologia. A vítima, Cauã Kildery, de 19 anos, contou que havia saído da aula há pouco tempo e estava caminhando na rua para casa quando foi abordado pelo homem com uma faca. Ele disse que tentou fugir, mas o homem conseguiu segurá-lo pela mochila.

"Quando eu virei de frente, foi quando ele tentou dar umas facadas, e a gente foi meio que numa certa luta, porque eu também não queria morrer, minha única preocupação ali era sair vivo", contou Cauã Kildery ao g1 . Os dois entraram em briga corporal e caíram no chão, momento no qual Cauã acabou atingido pela faca próximo ao ombro.

"Quando eu consegui ver que o bandido não tava mais com a faca, que a faca caiu no chão, foi quando ele pegou e arrancou o celular da minha mão", relembra.

Pouco depois, um segurança da universidade percebeu a confusão e se aproximou, mas o assaltante conseguiu fugir ainda assim, levando o celular do jovem.

A Secretaria da Segurança Pública e Defesa Social do Ceará (SSPDS) afirmou que a Polícia Militar foi acionada e esteve no local . A pasta também orientou a vítima a comparecer presencialmente à 10ª Delegacia de Polícia Civil da Capital para repassar mais informações que auxiliem à investigação.

Cauã Kildery ficou com machucados pelo corpo devido à luta corporal e sangrando devido à facada. Ele contou que o corte foi pequeno, mas profundo, e precisou de alguns pontos. Ele foi levado a um hospital por um familiar.

"A minha indignação foi que eu perdi meu celular, fiquei ferido, e meio que o esforço ali valeu a pena por eu ter ficado vivo, mas ficou aquele sentimento totalmente de revolta, porque eu não me senti, como eu posso dizer, assistido", reclama.

A Universidade Federal do Ceará afirmou também que "se solidariza com a vítima e lamenta que um membro da comunidade universitária tenha sido afetado pela violência urbana. Ao mesmo tempo, a instituição se coloca à disposição do estudante e das autoridades para qualquer apoio necessário".

Problemas de insegurança são reclamação recorrente dos estudantes campus de Porangabuçu da UFC, onde estão cursos como Farmácia, Odontologia, Medicina e Enfermagem. Em 2025, um estudante também foi esfaqueado durante uma tentativa de assalto na região. Em 2017, o campus chegou a registrar um sequestro-relâmpago.

A situação gerou protestos de alunos e servidores, que há anos reclamam de problemas de insegurança na área.

Ao g1 , a estudante de Odontologia, Talyta Lima , contou que estava na aula quando soube do assalto a Cauã. Ela, que já trabalha como técnica de enfermagem, prestou socorro de imediato para tentar limpar a ferida causada pela faca.

"O campus de Porangabuçu, o campus da saúde, já é conhecido por ser perigoso", contou. Ela conta que, para ir até ao Restaurante Universitário, a algumas quadras de distância, os estudantes pegam um ônibus que passou a ser fornecido pela UFC. "A gente conseguiu um ônibus que leva a gente só pra almoçar, pra você ver como é perigoso", lamenta.

articles.title: Tom Aspinall’s UFC Heavyweight Title Reign in Jeopardy? Dana White Gives His Answer
articles.summary: With his last outing coming at UFC 321 in October 25 last year, Tom Aspinall's title reign could actually come to an end outside the Octagon.
articles.body:
The UFC heavyweight division has been stuck in a bit of a limbo ever since Jon Jones became champion. While "Bones" defended his title just once between March 2023 and June 2025, fans were hoping things would finally change when Tom Aspinall was elevated to undisputed champion following Jones' retirement.

Unfortunately, Aspinall's first title defense at UFC 321 on October 25, 2025, only created more controversy. The Englishman was hit with a brutal double eye poke from Ciryl Gane and has been on the sidelines ever since. Aspinall was later diagnosed with the rare bilateral traumatic Brown's syndrome and has since undergone double eye surgery .

Now, nearly a year later, there is still no clear timeline for when the Englishman will return to the Octagon. Eddie Hearn recently revealed that Aspinall has undergone four surgeries since the injury and still needs to undergo a few more tests before he can be considered 100% healthy.

That has naturally led to speculation that Aspinall may never compete inside the Octagon again. Dana White recently shut down those rumors , but his latest comments about the heavyweight champion's inactivity have raised another question.

During a recent Zuffa Boxing post-fight press conference, White was asked whether Aspinall could be stripped of the 265-pound title if his absence continues.

While White didn't confirm that the UFC would take that route, Valentina Shevchenko's recent decision to vacate her flyweight title after suffering a ligament injury has certainly raised some eyebrows. Shevchenko, who last fought on November 15 at UFC 322, recently gave up her women's flyweight belt after her injury, leading some to wonder if Aspinall could eventually be asked to do the same.

White said, "We'll definitely be talking about that. Valentina doesn't want to tie up the division, and I'm assuming Tom feels the same way. I don't know personally where he is health-wise with everything, but we should clear that up soon."

White didn't outright say that Aspinall will be stripped or asked to vacate the title. Still, his comments make it clear that the UFC plans to have a conversation about the heavyweight champion's future sooner rather than later.

It's worth noting that Aspinall announced he was back to full training in June after Gane beat Alex Pereira at UFC Freedom 250 to claim the interim heavyweight title. Aspinall was even ready to fight Gane at UFC Paris on September 5. Yet that fight never came together, suggesting something may have changed behind the scenes.

Next month will mark a full year since Aspinall last stepped inside the Octagon. Even before this latest layoff, the Englishman had fought just twice since UFC 304 in July 2024 . He also holds the distinction of being the longest-reigning interim champion in UFC history.

Now, with another lengthy absence piling up, Aspinall's inactivity woes continue to hang over the heavyweight division. The big question is whether the UFC will continue waiting for its champion or eventually decide that the division simply can't afford to remain frozen any longer.

articles.title: Manguelo: “Hemos trazado un plan para llegar a la UFC”
articles.standfirst: El joven peleador español se enfrenta a Ángel Amaya este sábado en Guanches Warrior Championship
articles.summary: El joven peleador español se enfrenta a Ángel Amaya este sábado en Guanches Warrior Championship
articles.body: Tiene 24 años y a su edad, no hay muchos peleadores en España que generan la expectativa que levanta Miguel Navarro ‘Manguelo’ (4-0) cada vez que se prepara para un combate. El luchador del Climent Club está invicto y busca este 19 de septiembre una nueva victoria en el debut de la Guanches Warrior Championship de Hecher Sosa como promotora. Antes de viajar a Lanzarote, ‘Manguelo’ atiende a MARCA. Pregunta. ¿Por qué pelear en Guanches Warrior Championship? ¿Qué te convence? Respuesta. Mira, pues la verdad es que salió de la forma más natural posible. Estaba yo un día en WOW y estaba allí Hecher. Tenemos buena relación, nos conocemos desde hace varios años ya. Y estábamos ahí charlando y salió el tema que iba a hacer una promotora y tal… y salió natural. Le dije, ‘hostia, pues a mí me gustaría pelear ahí’. Y dijo: ‘pues a mí me encantaría que estuvieras’. Acabé mi pelea en WAR, empezamos a hablar por WhatsApp, por teléfono y se cerró todo así, la verdad, sin managers de por medio ni nada, hablando directamente él y yo. Y bueno, pelear ahí, pues, ¿por qué no?. El primer evento de Hecher, sabía que iba a estar chulo, que lo iba a hacer bien, ¿por qué no?. Una pelea más. P. Se mide a un 4-1 como Ángel Amaya. ¿Qué espera del combate? Se ha calentado un poco el tema por redes sociales… R. Las expectativas son siempre las mismas: ganar de la forma más espectacular posible, y estoy seguro que así va a ser. Si pudiera ser otra finalización en primer asalto, ya encadenaría un 5-0 con toda finalizaciones en primer asalto, que si me preguntas a mí creo que es lo que va a acabar pasando. Y el tema de que se haya calentado por redes sociales, la verdad, no por mí, a mí no me gusta esto, yo no suelo entrar en estas cosas, pero el chaval ha entrado a tope, de hecho se ha puesto en el récord de Instagram rollo Ilia con un 5-1… cuando tiene un 4-1. Yo cuando lo oí dije, ‘hostia, lo primero que va a tener que hacer al salir de la jaula es tener que cambiarse eso de la biografía’... pero bueno, las expectativas que tengo sinceramente es lo que te he comentado: ganar de la forma más espectacular posible y yo creo que va a ser en el primer asalto. P. No es usted un peleador dado a muchas polémicas fuera del octágono… R. Trabajo mis redes y trabajo mi imagen porque al final yo creo que eso es una de las partes fundamentales hoy en día, yo creo que la nueva generación de las artes marciales mixtas viene con eso y gracias a eso he tenido oportunidades que quizás no hubiera obtenido. Puedo vivir del deporte yo creo que en parte por mis resultados y en parte gracias a cómo yo he cuidado mi imagen. Pero sí, la verdad que no es mi estilo ponerme a insultarme con mi rival cuando realmente es que no es nada personal porque no lo conozco de nada. Voy a compartir con él la jaula el día 19 y nada más, entonces tener que forzar las cosas a mí la verdad que no me va mucho. P. Cada vez que usted pelea se generan expectativas. ¿Siente la presión? R. Sí, sí que siento que hay una expectativa cada vez que subo a pelear, y la presión al final yo creo que es algo que es inevitable y que es necesario. La presión al final crea los diamantes y estar sometido a presión desde el principio de mi carrera y a expectativas puestas en mí yo creo que a largo plazo es bueno. P. ¿En qué momento se da cuenta de que esto va en serio y que pelear será su vida? R. El día en el que yo me di cuenta que yo quería que esto estuviera vinculado a mi vida, dedicarme a esto, fue el día que hice mi debut en amateur. Ese día, la verdad, disfruté. En 2021. Ese día fue el que yo me di cuenta que yo quería dedicarme a esto y aparte yo tenía muchos ejemplos en mi gimnasio en el que yo veía que era posible. Yo ahí entrenaba todos los días con Ilia, que era ya peleador de la UFC. Entonces, desde antes yo ya entrenaba como un profesional. Yo entrenaba dos veces al día, todos los días, estaba todo el día en gimnasio, desde antes de mi debut en amateur. P. ¿Qué tal le va con Iridium? Es una de las agencias de representación más grande del mundo… R. Sí, de hecho es la que más peleadores lleva a UFC en todo el mundo. La verdad que súper bien, es algo con lo que estoy encantado y creo que ha sido un cambio positivo en mi carrera. Dentro de la propia agencia, hay varios managers. Yo con suerte estoy con Jason House, hablo con él prácticamente todas las semanas y hemos trazado un plan para mi carrera, para llegar a UFC. Y la verdad que tener a alguien que te lo dice de palabra, pero también ves que lo ha hecho con infinidad de peleadores, que ha cumplido las cosas que dice, pues la verdad que me da una motivación extra y me da la tranquilidad de que si yo cumplo por mi parte, el destino que es UFC… va a llegar, seguro. P. ¿Se puede contar algo de ese plan? R. Sí, bueno, a ver, al final la cosa es ir encadenando victorias y bueno, es que no puedo decir mucho, pero bueno, básicamente ir encadenando victorias. P. ¿Cómo está lo de pelear en WOW? R. Obviamente WOW es una plataforma que está haciendo las cosas muy bien, y yo creo que desde España es la plataforma número uno para llegar a UFC. Ahora mismo, como te digo, estoy muy centrado en esta pelea, no estoy pensando más allá de eso, pero la verdad que gracias a Dios tengo súper, súper, súper buenas ofertas de muchas promotoras del mundo. Fuera de UFC prácticamente tengo ofertas de todas… entonces, cuando acabe esta pelea voy a tomar una decisión y ver bien qué hago. Pero sí, WOW es una plataforma a considerar un montón, la verdad que ahora mismo para llegar al UFC desde España yo creo que es la reina. P. Se viene una quinta pelea en año y medio para usted. ¿Va todo muy rápido o ha podido pararse a reflexionar? R. Sí, es cierto que va a un ritmo muy rápido porque mi vida básicamente ahora mismo se basa en pelear, entrenar y empalmar unos campamentos con otros. Pero sí que me he parado a pensarlo y he cumplido muchos objetivos que yo tenía antes: principalmente vivir el deporte. Bueno, antes de ser profesional ya podía vivir el deporte, pero sí, me lo he parado a pensar y digo, ‘Wow, mi yo de 15-16 años cuando empezó con esto, lo veía como una meta lejana el vivir del deporte y ahora mismo pues es un objetivo cumplido’. Estoy seguro que mi yo de 15-16 años me miraría ahora mismo, y sería una persona a la que admiraría. Hemos recorrido un largo camino y esto nada más que empezar. P. ¿Cómo empezó todo? R. Yo empecé en judo con 5 años. Luego con 7 años judo empecé a competir, llegué a ser subcampeón del ranking nacional de infantil, gané varias Supercopas de España, gané Copas de España… tuve el certificado de deportista de élite de judo y luego me desenganché bastante del deporte, no me veía nada relacionado con los deportes de contacto. Pero ahí conocí las MMA. Yo vivía en Murcia, en un internado, pero como tenía el certificado de deportista de élite me dejaban salir para entrenar; entonces, yo ahí hacía lucha cuatro días a la semana y luego hacía MMA viernes y sábado. Ya cuando salí del internado, como con 17-18 años, me puse al 100% en MMA y un año después fue cuando debuté. Pero sí, prácticamente toda mi vida he estado ligado a deportes de contacto. P. ¿Cómo se definiría como peleador? R. Mira, es cierto que yo siempre he tirado por el grappling, por la lucha… sobre todo si me preguntaras unos años atrás, te hubiera dicho que soy claramente un peleador de grappling o de lucha, pero ahora mismo me siento un peleador súper completo. Sí, es cierto que yo soy un peleador de grappling súper, súper dinámico y peligroso en todas las posiciones, tengo finalizaciones de todos lados y yo creo que es divertido de ver. Yo creo que lo bueno de un peleador es saber adaptarse a todas las situaciones, pero sí, está claro que al final la MMA no es un deporte convencional como tal, es un espectáculo, es un show. Al final la UFC es una empresa privada y está claro que buscan gente que dé espectáculo… pero al final, lo que yo creo que es lo más importante es ganar. articles.title: Conor Benn confronts his future options after crushing loss to Ryan Garcia: 'What next? I don't have the answer'
articles.summary: Conor Benn lost his bid for the WBC welterweight world title inside two crushing rounds when he fought Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas; Benn is left considering his next options but says: "The truth is, I don't have the answer"; Moving back to middleweight is a likely route for him
articles.body:
Benn was attempting to follow in his famous father Nigel's footsteps and become a world champion when he challenged Garcia for the WBC belt at the T-Mobile Arena.

But Garcia, a top-class fighter, handed Benn a crushing loss when he dropped and stopped him in their second round.

"Everybody keeps asking: 'What's next for Conor Benn?'" he stated on social media. "The truth is, I don't have the answer.

"If you'd asked the 19-year-old version of me whether I thought I'd be standing here 10 years later, having lived through everything I have, I'd have told you that you were crazy.

"I train hard. I sacrifice. I've given this game 110 per cent every time I've stepped through those ropes, I've wanted to give people unforgettable nights and entertain.

"That's what this has always been about for me.

"People spend their hard-earned money to come and watch guys like us fight. I've never taken that for granted. I've always wanted to be a servant of the public and give everything I have when it matters."

The signs are that he will rest, recover and take some time out before considering how to return.

"Giving everything comes at a cost," he continued. "And the people who have paid that cost more than anyone are my family and my kids.

"They've sacrificed time with their dad so I could chase this dream. They've had to share me with this sport their entire lives.

"So when people ask me what's next for Conor Benn, right now the answer is simple.

He added: "Fight fans, thank you. Those who travelled to Vegas, those who stayed up until the early hours. I will never take your support for granted, especially on those nights things don't go to plan."

Benn is only 29 years old, so while he might take some time out of boxing, he can be expected to return to the sport.

The bout with Garcia was his first fight at welterweight in over four years. After two middleweight bouts with Chris Eubank Jr, the drop back to 147lbs was severe.

All the indications are that Benn will seek to go back up in weight. He could bypass 154lbs altogether and bounce back to middleweight.

There are title belt holders at 160lbs who have championships but relatively low profiles. Aaron McKenna, the IBF champion, and Denzel Bentley, now the WBO titleholder, for instance would surely welcome a fight with Benn if he could get ranked.

Perhaps he could move even higher in weight, even though he'd be small at middleweight let alone super-middle. But having a trilogy bout with Eubank Jr at 168lbs could make sense. It would save Eubank the punishing weight cut he had at middleweight with a rehydration clause and the two are 1-1 in their series.

For Benn, his Las Vegas adventure ended in a crushing defeat to Garcia, but there will be options for him as and when he chooses to return.

articles.title: Tom Aspinall vacates UFC heavyweight championship as he seeks to recover from on-going eye issues
articles.summary: Tom Aspinall has announced that he will vacate the UFC heavyweight title; Aspinall hasn't fought since October 2025 when his defence against Ciryl Gane ended as a no contest after he was poked in the eyes; Aspinall is still trying to recover from his injuries
articles.body:
Britain's Aspinall hasn't fought since October 2025 when his defence against Ciryl Gane ended as a no contest due to an eye poke.

Aspinall has had multiple medical procedures to address ongoing issues with his eyes since then but is still not ready to return to competition.

He has decided to vacate his title in the meantime.

"Ongoing eye complications mean I cannot get cleared to fight right now," Aspinall said. "I've had multiple surgeries, accidents and infections, and done everything possible to get back to competing.

"I know there has been questions about why I have been quiet. I have always followed the advice of the UFC and focused on my recovery while we've tried to make this happen.

"I have now made the decision to vacate the heavyweight title. I asked the UFC to allow me to make this statement because I don't want to hold the heavyweight division up.

"I know what it's like to have your career put on hold and I want the other fighters to have the opportunity to compete for the title."

He added: "We have worked closely with different doctors and specialists to try and make my return happen but, unfortunately, it is simply not possible right now.

"I am absolutely gutted. I have chased this dream since I was 10 years old."

articles.body: Pese a los anuncios de Dana White, jefe de la UFC, declarando la semana pasada que Ilia Topuria (17-1) estaba "listo para volver a pelear"... desde el equipo del 'Matador' se pide calma. 2026 es una fecha imposible para ver el regreso del doble campeón hispanogeorgiano después de perder ante Justin Gaethje (28-5) y sufrir lesiones en los orbitales, el tabique nasal y uno de sus pies. Ilia Topuria no está de campamento, no tiene fecha de pelea... y es poco probable que la conozca pronto. En este momento, una pelea de regreso no es nuestra prioridad", explica Gallo, uno de los hombres que mejor conoce el físico de Ilia Topuria. Los pasos que se están dando, comenta, son los adecuados: "Sinceramente, Ilia está progresando increíblemente bien, pero aún no hemos iniciado un campamento de entrenamiento propiamente dicho. Ni siquiera hemos empezado de verdad a hacer ningún tipo de entrenamiento de MMA todavía". Por lo tanto, como ya explicamos en MARCA, hay que ir con calma. articles.title: Tom Aspinall Vacates UFC Title After Infections, Surgeries and 'Complications with My Eye'
articles.summary: Tom Aspinall announced Monday he vacated the UFC heavyweight title due to "ongoing complications with my eyes."
articles.body:
Tom Aspinall announced Monday he vacated the UFC heavyweight title due to "ongoing complications with my eyes."

"I had previously agreed to a fight date and was back sparring, feeling great and ready to compete when an accident caused further damage to my right eye," he said. "This means more time away from the sport, and right now, the timing of my return is unclear."

Aspinall said that uncertainty left him with no other choice.

"I've now made the decision to vacate the heavyweight title," he said. "I've asked the UFC to allow me to make this statement because I don't want to hold the heavyweight division up. I know what it's like to have your career put on hold and I want the other fighters to have the opportunity to compete for the title."

Aspinall fought Ciryl Gane to a no contest at UFC 321 last October. The fight ended in the first round after Gane inadvertently poked him in the eye.

Uncrowned's Petesy Carroll reported in February that Aspinall was continuing to have trouble with his vision. He "can't track moving targets" and "struggles to do the most basic drills."

The 33-year-old underwent double eye surgery that month. By June, he said he was fully training again and hopeful of staging a rematch with Gane. Further setbacks forced him to alter those plans.

The status of the heavyweight belt is now up in the air. Gane beat Alex Pereira at UFC Freedom 250 in June to become the interim champion.

The UFC may simply remove the interim tag and make Gane the undisputed champion in the wake of Monday's news.

Aspinall is 15-3 as a pro and won eight of his first nine fights with the UFC prior to suffering his eye injuries. He insisted in his announcement he's not retiring altogether.

"Stepping away from the title is not stepping away from the sport or the dream," he said. "I'll continue doing everything I can to get healthy, get cleared and get back to competing as soon as possible."

Tom Aspinall, the reigning UFC heavyweight champion, announced early Monday that he would be vacating his title as he continues to deal with eye issues stemming from a double eye poke suffered at the hands of Ciryl Gane last October.

"I've now made the decision to vacate the heavyweight title," Aspinall posted on Instagram. "I've asked the UFC to allow me to make this statement because I don't want to hold the heavyweight division up. I know what it's like to have your career put on hold and I want the other fighters to have the opportunity to compete for the title."

Aspinall was forced to retire in the first round of the main event of UFC 321 after Gane's fingers went knuckle-deep into Aspinall's eyes. What was expected to be a life-changing fight for Aspinall turned into a nearly yearlong nightmare that is still continuing. Four months after the incident, Aspinall was still struggling to track moving targets and struggled with daily tasks.

Aspinall said he was nearing a potential return to fighting, having returned to sparring and was feeling "great," but a setback causing more damage to his right eye forced him to make this decision.

"Ongoing complications with my eyes mean I cannot get medically cleared to fight right now," Aspinall wrote. "I've had multiple surgeries, accidents and infections, and done everything possible to get back to competing. I know there have been questions about why I've been quiet. I've always followed the advice of the UFC and focused on my recovery while we've tried to make this happen."

The British heavyweight was on a three-fight winning streak and sported a 15-3 overall record before the Gane bout. While Aspinall's return is unclear, he does hope to fight again in UFC.

articles.standfirst: El peleador brasileño ha elogiado a 'El Matador' ahora que le ha dejado libre el camino para ser campeón de peso pluma
articles.summary: El peleador brasileño ha elogiado a 'El Matador' ahora que le ha dejado libre el camino para ser campeón de peso pluma
articles.body: Jean Silva es el nombre del momento en el peso pluma de la UFC. El peleador brasileño de los 'Fighting Nerds' sometió a José Delgado este pasado sábado en UFC Noche para ganar enteros de cara a pelear por el cinturón en su siguiente combate. Además, también ha hablado sobre la figura de Ilia Topuria, elogiando sus habilidades y agradeciendo que haya subido a peso ligero para no tener que medirse contra él. El 17 de febrero de 2024 Topuria se convirtió en campeón del peso pluma de la UFC tras noquear a Alexander Volkanovski, el actual monarca de la división. De hecho, hasta la fecha el peleador hispanogeorgiano ha sido el único capaz de vencer a 'Volk' en las 145 libras. Tras noquear a Max Holloway ese mismo año para defender por primera vez el título, 'El Matador' decidió subir a peso ligero para ser doble campeón, algo que conseguiría a posteriori. Por esa época Silva todavía no era la superestrella que es ahora, y cuando ascendió en los ránkings ya era demasiado tarde para medirse a Ilia. Sin embargo, no es algo que le ponga triste, ya que sabe del poder que tiene. "Pensando en Topuria... Gracias a Dios que dejó mi categoría. ¿Estás loco? Ese tipo está en otro nivel. Yo paso", reconoció antes de subir al octágono en el UFC Noche. Lo cierto es que hubo una época en la que el discurso era completamente diferente. De hecho, hace un año 'Lord' concedió una entrevista a MARCA y habló de cómo había logrado imitar el estilo de Ilia. "Yo sé imitar muy bien a Topuria, sé todo lo que hace. Porque fue campeón en mi categoría y ya hizo cosas que yo voy a hacer. Es normal que yo quiera ser como él en ciertos momentos. Pero voy a hacerlo mejor, de manera diferente. Si miras mis peleas, son mucho más rápidas. Él tardó cuatro años en disputar el cinturón; yo no llevo ni dos y ya voy a pelear por él. No me da vergüenza decir que sigo el camino de Topuria, lo imito en varias cosas. Hay que copiar a quienes hacen bien su trabajo. Y él hizo cosas grandiosas. Es normal querer parecerse a los que están arriba. Igual que Neymar en su día quiso ser como Cristiano Ronaldo, y mira dónde está ahora, uno de los grandes", afirmó en su momento el peleador brasileño. De hecho, incluso se atrevió a retarle a volver a bajar de categoría, diciendo que "si baja, me va a encontrar delante. Y ahí verán el gran estrago que pasará". Un año da para mucho, ya que a Silva le tocó vivir la cara amarga de la derrota contra Diego Lopes que le puso con los pies en la tierra. Se ha dado cuenta de dónde está el nivel de cada uno, y ahora prefiere mantenerse lo más alejado posible de una de las mayores superestrellas de la UFC.

articles.title: Tom Aspinall couldn't escape the curse of the UFC heavyweight championship
articles.summary: With Tom Aspinall's decision to vacate the belt, the timeline of events in the UFC heavyweight division over the past five years becomes even more ludicrous.
articles.body:
It's hard not to feel for Tom Aspinall. The man simply can't catch a break. This morning he vacated his UFC title as a courtesy to the rest of the heavyweight division, explaining in a post on social media that his eyes aren't fully healed from being gouged by Ciryl Gane last October at UFC 321.

You might remember that Aspinall had to wait 15 months just to get that fight with Gane, as he was subjected to the whims and whimsies of Jon Jones, the previous titleholder who coughed up the belt only after a yearlong deliberation.

That means that in the prime years of his career, Aspinall, now 33, has fought just once in 26 months. Right now he's unable to see his return, so he vacated.

Which brings us to the status of the UFC's heavyweight division …

Heavyweight right now is a trip. And when I say that I mean it's been a peyote trip, in which new faces keep leaping out of the fire, and any footholds on reality are tenuous at best. At first it was the ancestors we were seeing — Stipe Miocic, Francis Ngannou and eventually Jon Jones. Then Jones shapeshifted into Aspinall before our eyes, before morphing into the recurring face of Gane, a past trauma that won't go away. It gets trippier when Alex Pereira pops up from the bushes, firing arrows at Gane.

But seriously, look at this ludicrous timeline of events in the heavyweight division over the past five years. It's like an infinity picture that just keeps zooming out forever.

March 27, 2021 - UFC 260: Ngannou wins the lineal UFC heavyweight title by beating Miocic in a rematch. In many ways, this felt like a coronation for Ngannou, who'd seemed destined to one day win the belt since beginning his career 6-0 in the UFC, with six finishes. The first signs of trouble occurred when the UFC asked Ngannou to defend his title at UFC 265 against Derrick Lewis just four and a half months later, a turnaround that was too quick for Ngannou's tastes. He asked for a little more time, which rubbed the UFC the wrong way.

So, the UFC came up with a Plan B, booking Lewis into an interim title fight with Gane at UFC 265.

Aug. 7, 2022 - UFC 265: Gane beats Lewis via third-round TKO in Lewis' hometown of Houston to become the division's lesser champion, and to set up a heavyweight unification bout with Ngannou.

Jan. 22, 2022 - UFC 270: Ngannou needs all five rounds to unify the heavyweight titles, but he beats Gane going away. The fact that he used wrestling to get it done was the story, after suffering a knee injury in the early going. We eventually come to find out, UFC CEO Dana White was actively rooting against Ngannou . This is the last time things will ever be normal in this division again.

Jan. 14, 2023: After failing to come to terms on a new contract, the UFC strips Ngannou of his heavyweight belt and waives its one-year matching rights clause, which enables Ngannou to sign with the PFL and to pursue boxing. Ngannou, MMA's lineal heavyweight champion, gives Tyson Fury a scare in his boxing debut, which is a wild development in the broader world of combat sports.

Yet for UFC fans, the bottom line is that the lineal heavyweight champion is gone .

March 4, 2023 - UFC 285: With Ngannou skedaddling, Jon Jones — who after many years of flirting with a move to heavyweight — finally makes the leap, taking on former interim heavyweight champion Gane for the vacant title. Jones needs only two minutes and change to put away Gane with a guillotine choke and to win a title in a second weight class.

Still, because Jones didn't beat Ngannou, there are asterisks being flung around like so many ninja stars.

Nov. 11, 2023 - UFC 295: Jones was supposed to face former champion Miocic at Madison Square Garden, yet a torn pectoral muscle forces him out of action. Miocic isn't interested in fighting a replacement, so that means another interim title fight, this time between Tom Aspinall and Sergei Pavlovich. Aspinall beats Pavlovich in 69 seconds by knockout, making him the undisputed interim heavyweight champion to the non-lineal champ, Jones.

July 27, 2024 - UFC 304: With Dana White staunchly defending Jones as not only MMA's GOAT, but as the best pound-for-pound fighter in the world at every press junket he finds himself in, the UFC preserves the Jones-Miocic fight against hurricane-force blowback from fans and media. To keep things moving at heavyweight, Aspinall defends the interim title against Curtis Blaydes, which is a ludicrous thing to type. Interims are meant to be temporary!

In any case, he avenges his only loss in the UFC by knocking Blaydes out in 60 seconds.

Still, there are asterisks being juggled like tennis balls because Blaydes wasn't Jones (who hadn't beat Ngannou).

Nov. 16, 2024 - UFC 309: The stubborn heavyweight title fight between Jones and 42-year-old Miocic takes place at Madison Square Garden, a full year beyond its expiry, and Jones beats the shell of Miocic via third-round TKO . Jones retains the heavyweight title, paving the way for a unification bout with the now long-tenured interim titleholder, Aspinall.

The next six or eight months (or whatever): Jones iterates and reiterates that he has no interest in fighting Aspinall, as it does nothing for his legacy. Aspinall waits while Jones hits ports in Vietnam and Thailand, riding around on little motorbikes, saying things like, "living my best life." The UFC sticks by Jones as long as it can.

June 2025: As Aspinall watches the pages of his calendar flip through the seasons' many breezes, Jones finally vacates the title and announces his retirement from MMA . A couple of weeks later, when he catches wind that the UFC is planning an event on the White House lawn to celebrate America's 250th birthday, Jones changes his mind. This is the kind of event that would speak to his legacy. Jones wants to fight! On that card! Maybe against Alex Pereira! Wouldn't that be sick?!

(Dana doesn't think so; he says there's a one-in-a-billion chance Jones gets on that card, which doesn't deter Jones from lobbying.)

Oct. 25, 2025 - UFC 321: With the lineal champ Ngannou long gone and the non-lineal champ Jones now out of the picture, the stand-in champ Aspinall has the "interim" tag lifted from his title, and now finds himself the main man at heavyweight. Because he inherited the throne without beating Jones (or Ngannou), there are asterisks in the sky outnumbering the stars in heaven.

That means the UFC books him against … you guessed it, Gane. The fight takes place in Abu Dhabi, and is meant to get the division moving again. Instead, toward the end of a competitive first round, Gane's fingers end up knuckle-deep inside of Aspinall's eye sockets, which brings the fight to a crashing halt.

The crowd boos. White discounts the injury . And Aspinall, left to defend himself more fiercely than he did any title, spends the next few months trying to prove that his eyes are in bad shape.

June 14, 2026 - UFC Freedom 250: With the now disputed heavyweight champion Aspinall on the mend, the UFC opts to book an interim heavyweight title between the one-time interim champion Gane and the two-division champion Pereira, who is moving to heavyweight to become the first fighter in UFC history to win titles in three weight classes. Gane scores a TKO victory over Pereira , yet many are left talking about the series of illegal blows he landed to the back of Pereira's head.

Pereira spends the next few months roasting referee Herb Dean on a spit , while Gane steals off like a thief in the night with his second interim title, ready for a rematch. At this point, Gane's record in lineal title fights is 0-1, in non-lineal title fights is 0-1-1 NC, and in interim title fights is 2-0.

Sept. 14, 2026: Aspinall vacates the heavyweight title, and it's left for the UFC to decide whether to upgrade Gane to (hugely disputed) heavyweight champion status, or to have his next fight — either in the mulligan fight with Pereira, or with the schticky-yet-undefeated Josh Hokit — be for the vacant belt.

Between the original heavyweight champion Ngannou, the retired Jones, and the injured Aspinall, no titles are presently held yet no titles were ever lost. The UFC heavyweight belt has gone underground at this point, passing through subterranean hands with fingerprints all over it, none of which can be made out by the naked eye.

Forensics might have to be involved by the time it goes up for grabs again, but that's the current state of the UFC heavyweight division.

No one, especially not Tom Aspinall, could've foreseen how things would go from here. (Sarah Stier via Getty Images)
Nothing has ever been right since the double eye-poke of doom. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

articles.title: Dana White announces special $50,000 'proper chaos bonus' for UFC 331
articles.summary: A new bonus will be at play at Saturday's UFC 331.
articles.body:
One of the 26 fighters competing Saturday at UFC 331 will walk away with an extra $50,000 in their pocket.

UFC CEO Dana White announced on Monday there will be a special bonus in play during the event in Los Angeles. In honor of hit Paramont+ series "MobLand", there will be an extra bonus. That will be on top of the regular four $100,000 Fight Night bonuses – Fight of the Night (which is earned by two fighters in the most exciting bout), and two individual Performance of the Night awards.

White didn't reveal the exact criteria for the bonus or what exactly he'll be looking for, but he did name it the "proper chaos bonus" and said it'll be up to him to determine the winner.

"Long before I did a deal with Paramount, I've been telling you guys I'm a huge fan of 'Mobland,'" White said Monday in an Instagram video. "It is one of the best shows on television. Season two premieres this Friday on Paramount+, the night before UFC 331 in LA. So for one night only, we're bringing a little proper chaos into the octagon. At UFC 331, we are unlocking the proper chaos bonus. $50,000 awarded to the fighter who I think deserves it most. UFC 331, Van vs. Pantoja is live September 19th on Paramount+, and do not forget season two, premieres this Friday. Mobland, one of the best shows on television. Knockout season one, just in time for season two."

articles.title: Curtis Blaydes taking 'Chutes and Ladders' approach to UFC title
articles.summary: Curtis Blaydes only wants fights that will get him in the best position for a heavyweight title shot.
articles.body:
Curtis Blaydes believes he sent everyone a reminder at Noche UFC.

Following a loss in a gritty Fight of the Night war against Josh Hokit at UFC 327 in April, Blaydes (20-6 MMA, 15-6 UFC) returned to action to take on Waldo Cortes-Acosta on the main card of Noche UFC at Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Ariz. Blaydes got the job done on the scorecards against Cortes-Acosta (17-4 MMA, 10-4 UFC) to bounce back into the win column.

Blaydes admits he thought Cortes-Acosta would be more aggressive in the fight, which led to some slower moments. He said that during training camp, his preparation was centered around dealing with constant forward pressure, but the fight played out differently.

Now that he's back on track, Blaydes wants a top-tier heavyweight, whoever that may be. He's not looking closely at the rankings because Blaydes believes they don't make logical sense right now.

"I think I deserve a top 5 opponent," Blaydes said during a post-fight news conference ( h/t Cageside Press ). "There's a lot of these younger guys – no disrespect – I don't know a lot of their names. I know Mario Pinto, couple other guys, they've been slowly coming ahead of me. I'm like, 'Why am I sliding?' Yeah, I lost to Hokit, but it was a great fight. Even Hokit has been sliding. Rizvan (Kuniev)is ahead of me. I beat him. He gets top 5 after he beats Tyrell Fortune, who wasn't even ranked. Mario Pinto gets top 10 after he beats Ryan Spann, who's not even a real heavyweight.

"The rankings don't mean a damn thing to me no more. I no longer respect them. I'm not even going to look at them. That's why I don't really know where everyone is, but I hope to get a top 5 opponent next."

Blaydes recently signed a new eight-fight deal with the UFC, so he's not going anywhere soon. The 35-year-old former interim title challenger still has his eyes on gold, so he won't take fights against just anyone; opponents have to make sense for a title path.

"As we're getting older, we don't just want to be fighting anybody, because you could always get injured," Blaydes said. "You could break the hand, break the toe, break anything. So yeah, I'm not just fighting just anybody. Like, I took this fight because he was ranked above me, had a lot of steam, even though he just lost to Volkov. He's been very active, he's got a lot of highlights. That's why we took this fight in his hometown. I'm looking for, like I said, a top 5 guy.

"Like, I'm thinking about that game, Chutes and Ladders. As few steps as I can take to get here. If I can chute here, and chute here – that's what I'm looking to do. It just depends on the rankings, I guess."

articles.title: Donald Trump Jr and Bettina Trump say Putin ally paid for some wedding festivities as a 'gift'
articles.summary: An Instagram post from the couple said two nights of their wedding festivities in the Bahamas were partially funded by Umar Kremlev.
articles.body:
Donald Trump Jr.'s wife, Bettina Trump, confirmed that their May wedding was paid for in part by an ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin.

A post on her Instagram account - attributed to the couple - said that two nights of their three-day wedding festivities on a private island in the Bahamas were partially funded by Umar Kremlev, a Russian oligarch with close ties to Putin.

The statement was released Monday after investigative journalism outlet ProPublica published a story detailing that Kremlev paid "hundreds of thousands of dollars" for the celebration.

Donald Trump Jr., one of the US president's sons, is a private citizen, so it's not illegal for him to accept gifts from a foreign national.

"Our dear friend Umar very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations for us AFTER our wedding. It was an extraordinarily generous wedding gift from a friend, and something for which we were and remain incredibly grateful," the couple said in the statement.

But ethics watchdog groups said it still presented the appearance of a conflict of interest for the president's son to accept lavish gifts from someone associated with a foreign head of state - even if he is not a US government employee.

"People don't just give hundreds of thousands of dollars to a random acquaintance without wanting something," said Jordan Libowitz, vice president of communications for Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW).

"You can see how [Putin] would enjoy all this press about how people in his circle are cozying up to people in the president's circle."

According to the ProPublica article, the couple was married on a private island in the Bahamas, then held a two-day celebration on a separate island that rents for approximately $100,000 per night. Kremlev also paid other costs for the party, including a roughly $70,000 fireworks display, the report found.

Kremlev runs the International Boxing Association (IBA), an organization funded by the state-backed Gazprom energy company. The Olympic Committee suspended the group in part over its failure to report its ties to the Russian energy giant.

Earlier this year Kremlev was part of a delegation that visited China with Putin. The Russian president also gave Kremlev the Order of Friendship, a top state honor, according to ProPublica.

A spokesperson for Trump Jr. told the news outlet that the president's son and Kremlev were personal friends and did not have "a business relationship."

An ally of Trump Jr. referred the BBC to the Instagram statement.

In a statement to ProPublica, Kremlev's office said "Mr. Kremlev and Mr. Trump Jr have a friendly relationship." The statement said the men met a few years ago.

Kremlev attended part of the wedding, the outlet reported. Other attendees included one of the US president's daughters, Ivanka Trump, and her husband, Jared Kushner, who has worked for the US on diplomatic negotiations with Iran, Russia and in the Middle East.

The Trump campaign and family faced controversy for potential ties to Russia during the 2016 presidential election, resulting in a special counsel investigation. During the campaign Donald Trump Jr. brokered a meeting at Trump Tower with a Russian operative that was closely scrutinized during the probe.

Libowitz, of CREW, said either the president, who is a billionaire, or Trump Jr. -- who is worth $300 million, according to Forbes -- could have paid for the full wedding to avoid a conflict of interest.

"His father is worth billions he could have picked up the tab. Clearly they just didn't want to pay for it," Libowitz said. "They don't really care about the ethical ramifications."

articles.title: Cage or ring? Scott Coker reveals new MMA promotion’s name, massive 32-man Grand Prix
articles.summary: A new (Coker) era has begun. After months of anticipation, former Strikeforce founder and longtime Bellator president Scott Coker finally unveiled his brand-...
articles.body:
After months of anticipation, former Strikeforce founder and longtime Bellator president Scott Coker finally unveiled his brand-new mixed martial arts (MMA) promotion , along with several major details surrounding its format and expected 2027 launch ( watch here ).

Coker's new promotion is called Ki MMA (pronounced "key MMA"). In Japanese, ki can refer to spirit, energy or life force, which inspired the organization's official slogan: "Ki: The Force Within The Fighter."

Okay, now that we have the name, how exactly will this thing work?

Ki MMA will launch with an ambitious 32-man Featherweight World Grand Prix featuring fighters from four regions: North America, South America, Asia and Europe.

Each region will supply eight competitors who will advance through a series of qualifying events until one continental champion remains. Those four winners will then meet in the World Grand Prix finale, with the semifinal winners competing twice in one night to crown Ki MMA's inaugural Featherweight champion.

The fights will also take place inside a ring rather than a cage, separating Ki MMA from UFC, PFL and most other major promotions. According to Coker, staging MMA fights inside a ring is something he has wanted to do since his Strikeforce days.

Coker and longtime matchmaker Rich Chou did not announce any official roster signings during the presentation. However, the promotion plans to target promising fighters between 18 and 25 years old while remaining aggressive in the free-agent market.

"We have a budget that will allow us to get any free agents, so give us a call," Coker said.

Considering the new promotion reportedly launched with $60 million in financing , that phone could start ringing quickly.

While the 32-man Featherweight Grand Prix will be the centerpiece of Ki MMA's launch, Coker confirmed that its cards will also feature fights across other weight classes.

The promotion is expected to hold its inaugural event during the first quarter of 2027 . Potential markets under consideration include San Jose, Brazil, Japan, South Korea, France, Budapest and possibly Italy as Ki MMA attempts to establish itself as a truly global organization.

Several major questions remain unanswered, including the complete roster, broadcast partner, tournament prize and exact date and location of the inaugural event.

Nevertheless, Coker's vision is now clear: a global tournament, promising young talent, major free-agent signings and old-school MMA fights inside a ring.

In other words, this sounds extremely Scott Coker.

articles.title: Dustin Poirier’s untold life beyond the UFC: Inside the business ventures, family story and charity work behind the MMA icon
articles.summary: MMA News: Dustin Poirier built his name through some of the toughest fights in the UFC, but his story reaches far beyond the Octagon. The former interim lightwe.
articles.body: Dustin Poirier built his name through some of the toughest fights in the UFC, but his story reaches far beyond the Octagon. The former interim lightweight champion has created businesses, built a family and dedicated time to helping people in need. His journey outside MMA shows a different side of the fighter fans have watched for years. From a Louisiana-style Cajun hot sauce to his Rare Stash bourbon brand, Poirier has turned his public profile into opportunities beyond fighting. But among his biggest achievements is The Good Fight Foundation, which he created with his wife Jolie to support underserved communities.Dustin Poirier went beyond UFC fame with business ventures, family and The Good Fight FoundationPoirier’s long UFC career gave him a platform that extended well beyond fight nights. After years of competing against some of the biggest names in MMA, he began putting that recognition into businesses connected to his personality and Louisiana roots.In late 2020, Poirier launched a Louisiana-style Cajun hot sauce. The venture gave him a way to bring a piece of his home state into his growing business portfolio while creating another connection with his supporters.Two years later, he entered the bourbon business with Rare Stash. The brand added another commercial venture to a career that had already made Poirier one of the most recognizable fighters of his generation.Those businesses are an important part of understanding Poirier’s financial story. His earnings and estimated net worth are often discussed by celebrity wealth sites, although such figures are estimates rather than official financial disclosures.His UFC career remains the foundation of his public profile. Big fights against Conor McGregor, Justin Gaethje and Max Holloway helped establish Poirier as a major name in the sport. Still, his life away from competition has become just as interesting.His family and The Good Fight Foundation reveal the purpose behind Poirier’s successPoirier married Jolie LeBlanc in 2009, and the couple welcomed their daughter in 2016. Jolie has also played an important role in The Good Fight Foundation, making the organization a project closely connected to their family.The Good Fight began in 2018 with a simple idea. Poirier and Jolie started auctioning Dustin’s fight memorabilia instead of letting pieces from his career sit unused. The money was then directed toward people and communities that needed support.One early auction featured memorabilia from Poirier’s fight against Eddie Alvarez at UFC 211. The proceeds helped provide meals through a local food bank.The foundation eventually grew into a registered nonprofit with a much wider mission. Its work has included food insecurity, health care support, disaster relief and community projects.The organization has also developed strong ties to Lafayette, Louisiana. Its annual back-to-school efforts have provided hundreds of children with backpacks and school supplies, while other projects have supported families and children in need.Its work has not been limited to Louisiana. The foundation has also supported clean-water projects in Uganda and other charitable causes over the years.That side of Poirier’s life adds another layer to his UFC legacy. Fighting made him famous, but the foundation has allowed him to use that fame for something beyond competition.His businesses show his ambition outside MMA, while his family and charity work reveal what he has chosen to do with the platform he built.For Poirier, the legacy may ultimately be about more than his biggest victories or the money earned during his fighting career. articles.title: “Your life seems tied to breaking rules”: Islam Makhachev fires back at Jon Jones after doping dispute over 20-fight UFC win streak
articles.summary: MMA News: Islam Makhachev has responded to Jon Jones after the former UFC champion strongly defended his record following comments about his 20-fight unbeaten r.
articles.body: Islam Makhachev has responded to Jon Jones after the former UFC champion strongly defended his record following comments about his 20-fight unbeaten run. Makhachev had questioned whether Jones’ streak should be considered valid because of his past failed drug tests and suspensions.Jones hit back on social media and defended himself by referring to previous USADA findings. The exchange quickly turned personal, with Jones also mocking Makhachev’s only UFC loss and bringing up comments made by Makhachev’s late coach, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov.Islam Makhachev responds to Jon Jones after doping claim goes viral Islam Makhachev has now answered Jones with a sharp tweet. The UFC welterweight champion did not back away from his earlier comments and appeared to criticise Jones for repeatedly avoiding blame over controversies during his career.Makhachev wrote, “Your whole life seems to be tied to breaking the rules one way or another, and somehow, you’re never the one to be blamed.”The response came after Jones posted a lengthy defence of his UFC record. Jones argued that fans could not accept USADA’s findings about his failed test while ignoring the agency’s conclusion that the substance was not found to be performance-enhancing or intentional.Jones wrote, “If you believe USADA for finding a picogram in my system, then you must believe USADA when they say, ‘It was not found to be PERFORMANCE ENHANCING or INTENTIONAL.’ You can’t have it both ways.”The former UFC light heavyweight and heavyweight champion has faced two major doping controversies. He served suspensions after failed drug tests in 2017 and 2018. Jones has consistently denied intentionally using performance-enhancing drugs.His 2017 test involved a turinabol metabolite. Jones said the substance entered his system through a contaminated sexual enhancement product. In the 2018 case, an arbitrator also found that there was no evidence Jones had intentionally used steroids.However, Makhachev believes those incidents should affect how Jones’ famous winning streak is viewed.Jones responded by pointing to his long record inside the Octagon. He said his hand had been raised in every fight he completed without the disqualification against Matt Hamill.Jones then turned his attention to Makhachev’s only UFC defeat. The Russian lost to Adriano Martins by knockout in 2015.Jones had mocked that defeat in his response,he wrote, “Let’s not forget you’ve been KO’d, flatlined, went night night.”He also referenced Makhachev’s late coach and Khabib Nurmagomedov’s father, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. Jones reminded Makhachev that the respected coach had previously described him as a “gift from God.”The former champion also brought Daniel Cormier into the argument. Jones defeated Cormier twice, although their second fight was later changed to a no-contest after Jones tested positive for a turinabol metabolite.Makhachev currently sits at the top of the UFC pound-for-pound rankings, a position Jones previously held. The latest exchange could add another chapter to the ongoing debate over Jones’ legacy and whether his past doping cases should affect how his remarkable winning streak is viewed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Meanwhile, Ortega has confirmed that he hopes to return in November after suffering an injury around his right eye.Brian Ortega’s withdrawal leaves UFC 331 with a major changeFans became concerned about Brian Ortega after footage appeared to show him covering an injury around his right eye. The UFC later confirmed that the 35-year-old would not compete at this weekend’s event.Ortega was scheduled to face Renato Moicano in a lightweight rematch. articles.title: “It’s a shame”: Why did Michael Page feel disrespected at the end of his UFC journey despite a 5-1 record?
articles.summary: MMA News: Michael “Venom” Page’s UFC journey was supposed to be about proving that his unique style could work at the highest level of MMA. He arrived in the pr.
articles.body: Michael “Venom” Page’s UFC journey was supposed to be about proving that his unique style could work at the highest level of MMA. He arrived in the promotion with a reputation built on speed, creativity and spectacular finishes. By the time his UFC run ended, however, the conversation had changed. Page had won five of six fights, yet he felt the way his departure was handled did not match what he had achieved. His disappointment was not simply about losing a contract. It was about communication, respect and the feeling that he never got the chance to understand where he stood. Now, Page is reflecting on a chapter that taught him as much about himself as fighting.Michael Page believed his UFC record deserved a proper conversationPage joined the UFC in 2024 after becoming one of Bellator’s most recognizable fighters. His first appearance against Kevin Holland at UFC 299 gave fans an early look at what he could bring to the promotion.He won that fight by unanimous decision, using his movement and striking to frustrate Holland. While the spectacular finishes that had become part of Page’s identity did not arrive consistently afterward, the British veteran continued finding ways to win.His UFC record eventually reached 5-1. Four of those victories came consecutively, with his final win coming against Nursulton Ruziboev in Paris. From Page’s perspective, that record should have at least opened the door for another discussion with the promotion."I had goals to achieve, so regardless of anything, I was winning my fights, which says to me you get to stay," Page told Uncrowned. "That's the premise of this game. Success should breed more opportunities. So, I still felt like we'd sit down at the table.""What is the harm in allowing me to speak [after the fight]?" Page said. "I've seen fights that have been absolutely terrible, and they still get to go on the mic and say their piece. This is the second time it's happened to me."The way he eventually found out about his UFC future made the experience harder. Dana White later confirmed publicly that the promotion would not re-sign Page. Page was on vacation when he saw messages from people reacting to the news."I was just chilling on holiday, and I see I'm getting messages from people seeing the clip. OK, I guess that's where we're at," Page said.For Page, the bigger issue was not necessarily the decision itself. He said he would have accepted a difficult conversation if it had been handled directly."I'm always happy to have a conversation, regardless of if it's a difficult one or easy one. ... If you're not happy with the performances, have a conversation with me. ... At least it gives me a goal and something to work toward, and I know exactly where I stand with the partnership."The deeper part of Michael Page’s story goes beyond his UFC recordPage’s UFC experience also forced him to examine something more personal. Despite continuing to win, he felt he was not producing the performances he knew he was capable of delivering."I just know what I'm capable of, and for some reason, I don't know what it is, I just feel like I'm not pushing myself enough in the fights," Page said. "It's weird to say, because I'm winning fights and I'm not at my best. It's just a shame that I haven't been able to really showcase my best, and yet I'm still beating fighters that are at the top of their game.""I realized it second fight in, that I was carrying a weight, and I shouldn't be. It was a case of figuring out how to not do that when I'm heading into these fights. How to not fixate on performing the way that I used to and just enjoy the performance.""It's a show. I'm excited about the things I can do with my walkout, this and that. I can visualize exactly how amazing and epic that's going to be. There's nobody I'm saying no to right now," Page said.At 39, Page still wants to compete. More importantly, he appears determined to leave the frustration of his UFC exit behind and rediscover the enjoyment that made him fall in love with fighting in the first place.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Conor Benn comeback? WBO champion Denzel Bentley says Conor Benn can 'skip the queue' for middleweight world title shot
articles.summary: Conor Benn suffered a devastating two-round defeat in Las Vegas when he challenged Ryan Garcia for the WBC welterweight world title at the weekend; but Benn could now return to middleweight and WBO 160lb world champion Denzel Bentley has offered him a shot at his title
articles.body:
Denzel Bentley, the WBO world champion at 160lbs, is open to fighting Benn.

Benn twice boxed his family rival, Chris Eubank Jr, at middleweight before boiling back down to welterweight to challenge Ryan Garcia for the WBC title.

Garcia hammered Benn inside two rounds, with Benn now expected to return to middleweight.

Bentley, elevated to full world champion after claiming the WBO interim title with a storming performance against Endry Saavedra in April, would relish the prospect of defending his belt against Benn.

"Although the public might not think he deserves another world title shot in my eyes I feel like his profile is big enough for him to skip the queue," Bentley told Sky Sports .

"It's unfair but that's the sport we're in. Obviously it's beneficial for me, especially financially, so 100 per cent that's the fight I would take. I've never had any beef with Conor, we've always been cool.

"But if he is coming to the 160lb division, he goes from a companion to a potential challenger," he added.

"Firstly he needs to get himself right, well and fit. I think he should take a lot of time off and recover. I don't think there's any rush for him to get back into a boxing ring or even a gym. That weight cut was a fight in itself for him I think. Probably took a lot out of himself.

"Once he's well and fit, if he decides to move up to 160lbs and he does want the challenge, I think that's probably a conversation we can probably have ourselves: 'If you want to do this, let's push for it.'"

Bentley though had a warning for him. "I think I'm dangerous for anyone. I'm a lot bigger than him and I can punch."

But he added: "I think he will be a lot better with the extra weight.

"I think at 160lbs he'll be a lot more fuelled. But, listen, I punch as well and there were a lot of flaws in his game that night that I could exploit."

articles.title: Dana White confirma que su nuevo 'evento imposible' no será en el Monte Rushmore
articles.standfirst: El jefe de la UFC quiere seguir superándose, pero ha acallado los rumores de una posible cartelera en un lugar emblemático para los Estados Unidos
articles.summary: El jefe de la UFC quiere seguir superándose, pero ha acallado los rumores de una posible cartelera en un lugar emblemático para los Estados Unidos
articles.body: La UFC ha llegado a un punto en el que tiene muy difícil superarse en sus siguientes objetivos. Dana White -jefe de la compañía- ha llevado a la empresa al siguiente nivel en los últimos años, organizando carteleras en lugares inimaginables. Aun así, el mandamás de la promotora ha reconocido que quiere seguir realizando eventos en sitios únicos, y en las últimas semanas había surgido un rumor de una posible megacartelera en el mítico Monte Rushmore. Sin embargo, él mismo se ha encargado de desmentirlo. En septiembre de 2024, la UFC llevó a cabo un evento en 'La Esfera' de Las Vegas para conmemorar al pueblo mexicano en el UFC Noche. Mas allá de la cartelera numerada en sí, que contó con algunas de las caras más conocidas de la UFC, lo que más llamo la atención fue el espectáculo audiovisual. No fue un evento al uso, sino que por momentos los combates pasaron a un segundo plano por todo lo demás. Sin embargo, el propio White avisó que ese tipo de sucesos posiblemente no volverían a ocurrir por el elevado coste que suponen. Más tarde, el pasado 14 de junio, la UFC subió el listón y realizó una cartelera en la Casa Blanca con motivo del 250 Aniversario de la Independencia de los Estados Unidos. De nuevo, un evento irrepetible donde apenas hubo siete combates y donde Ilia Topuria perdió el invicto y el cinturón de peso ligero a manos de Justin Gaethje. Más allá de ese resultado, el enclave en sí dio pie a imágenes históricas para la promotora, que parecía que no podría superarse aún más. Dana White es un tipo ambicioso, y hace unas semanas anunció que ya se habían puesto manos a la obra para realizar otro evento en un lugar emblemático de Estados Unidos. Eso sí, no será el Monte Rushmore. "No, no va a ser el Monte Rushmore, pero espero dar noticias en las próximas semanas", reconoció en una entrevista con Pat McAfee. Para llegar a cabo eventos en lugares históricos, hacen falta muchas negociaciones y permisos que seguramente todavía no hayan finalizado, de ahí que el mandamás de la UFC prefiera ser cauto hasta que todos los acuerdos estén cerrados. Sin embargo, cuando anuncia algo suele cumplirlo, por lo que deben de quedar algunos flecos para poder hacer oficial el próximo gran paso de la empresa. No hay que olvidar que el propio Dana White confirmó que estuvieron cerca de organizar una cartelera en el Coliseo Romano para llevar a cabo un combate entre Elon Musk y Mark Zuckerberg, pero finalmente no pudieron conseguir los permisos ni reunir el dinero suficiente para poder cerrar el trato. Aún así, Dana dejó abierta la puerta a que algún inversor ponga dinero y se pueda realizar en un futuro. De momento, sus planes están centrados en Estados Unidos, por lo que hay varias especulaciones sobre qué lugar elegirán para este superevento que tienen entre manos. El Gran Cañón, la cárcel de Alcatraz o Central Park podrían ser algunos de los posibles lugares, pero hasta que no lo confirmen no hay que dar nada por hecho. Lo que está claro es que será otro evento para la historia de los deportes de contacto, tal y como vienen haciendo en los últimos años.
